Humanoids

ELSA Japan adds Booster K1 and T2, targeting November shipments

A Japanese distribution agreement brings humanoid research platforms alongside the company’s existing computing products.

ELSA Japan ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Japanese distribution begins

ELSA Japan announced a domestic distribution agreement with Booster Robotics on October 8, adding K1 and T2 for research, education and embodied-AI experiments. Shipments are planned for November 2026, with pricing available from sales. The news concerns a distribution channel, rather than the robots’ first global introduction.

Two platform levels

The distributor lists K1 at approximately 95 centimeters and 19.5 kilograms, with 22 degrees of freedom. T2 is approximately 140 centimeters tall and 42 kilograms, with a stated dual-arm payload of up to ten kilograms. T2 offers a Jetson Thor T5000 option, while its degrees of freedom vary with the selected hand configuration.

Configuration matters

Each platform has four variants differing in computing, battery or end-effector equipment. ELSA lists two hours of continuous walking for T2, without publishing equivalent results for every task. These are supplier specifications; researchers need to confirm the chosen configuration when designing experiments or evaluating deployment.
